analysis:
Examined all five primary analyses and every replayed source unit, including metadata, patches and numbered excerpts. Replay omits 16 reviewed units, so workflow/test claims in the analyses could not all be independently verified.
The provider build action adds SwiftPM repository caching and makes build, repository and Metal cache publication conditional on a default-off save-caches input (action.yml HEAD 107, 116, 143 in the patch). This narrows publication when callers enforce the reported master/dev push restriction. Credential persistence is disabled in component-changes.yml:36; the reported cached-checkout controls elsewhere require omitted workflow source for verification. Connectivity fsck is not cache provenance or configuration validation, but no supplied evidence establishes an adversarial cache writer reaching trusted builds; a poisoning finding is therefore unsupported.
The audio output is correctly forwarded from the classifier through job and reusable-workflow outputs (component-changes.yml:12-13,28). Its production and dependency closure remain unverified: scripts/ci-component-paths.py is absent, while docs/developer/test.md:148-154 describes newly conditional native audio coverage. Review that classifier together with ci.yml:400-418 and aggregate gates to ensure security-relevant media changes select the test and skipped execution is represented accurately. This matters to TB-007/T-050 and artifact qualification A-017/T-054.
Also retain review of sparse checkout versus provenance validation (docs-impact.yml HEAD 61-68), cached build source/toolchain binding, and preinstalled CMake verification described in changelog.d/ci-git-swiftpm-cache.md:7. Missing implementations do not establish regressions. No replayed change alters live authorization, attestation, hop encryption, billing, privileged-helper authority or T-041's production cache isolation/crypto. No independently supported finding qualifies; remaining uncertainty concerns CI integrity and reduced test coverage, not inferred runtime vulnerabilities.
